| **ICM** | Grade A — compact, tightly packed, clearly demarcated cell mass; high cellular density |

| **Blastocoel** | Well-formed cavity; fluid distribution appears symmetric |

### Favorable Patient Parameters
```
✅ Age 34 — below the critical 35-year threshold
✅ Normal BMI (24.9) — optimal implantation range
✅ FSH 5.2 IU/L — excellent ovarian reserve marker
✅ Excellent oocyte yield: 14/14 MII maturation rate (100%)
✅ Endometrial thickness 10.5mm — within optimal range (8–12mm)
✅ Male factor: treatable etiology; sperm parameters adequate
   → 52.2M/mL concentration (normal >16M)
   → 65.5% motility (normal >42%)
✅ First IVF cycle — no prior failure history
✅ Antagonist protocol — appropriate for this patient profile
```

## 3. Risk Factors & Favorable Indicators

### 🔴 Risk Factors
```
1. SMOKING (Current)
   • Reduces implantation rate by 15–40%
   • Impairs endometrial receptivity
   • Increases miscarriage risk significantly
   • Negatively affects oocyte quality long-term
   
2. Male Factor Etiology
   • Sperm DNA fragmentation not assessed
   • Morphology data absent
   • May contribute to embryo developmental competence issues
   
3. AMH Not Available
   • Cannot fully characterize ovarian reserve
   • 100% MII rate suggests good reserve but AMH needed
   
4. Sedentary Lifestyle
   • Walking only — suboptimal for metabolic optimization
   • Minor risk but modifiable
   
5. Alcohol Consumption
   • 1–3 drinks/week — light but not zero
   • Some evidence of negative implantation impact
```

### 🟢 Favorable Indicators
```
✓ Top-tier embryo quality (3AA)
✓ Age 34 with strong ovarian response
✓ 100% oocyte maturation rate
✓ Normal endometrial environment
✓ Low-stress lifestyle
✓ Good sperm parameters (concentration/motility)
✓ Normal BMI
✓ Fresh cycle with excellent reserve markers
```

```
ADJUSTED ESTIMATED RANGE:
```

## 5. Clinical Recommendations

### Immediate Transfer Cycle

```
TRANSFER RECOMMENDATIONS:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
□ Single embryo transfer (eSET) — age 34, first cycle, 
  high-quality blastocyst; avoid multiple pregnancy risk
  
□ Luteal phase support:
  → Progesterone vaginal suppositories (200mg TID)
  → Consider estradiol supplementation if FET protocol
  
□ Endometrial receptivity:
  → ERA test not mandatory for first cycle but consider 
    if this cycle fails
    
□ Timing: Proceed with transfer — morphology supports it
```

### ⚠️ Pre-Transfer Counseling Priorities

```
1. SMOKING CESSATION — URGENT
   ▸ Refer to cessation program immediately
   ▸ Evidence: Every cigarette smoked during luteal phase
     reduces implantation probability
   ▸ Consider cycle delay if patient can achieve 
     4–8 weeks cessation before transfer
   ▸ NRT safety in peri-transfer period to be discussed
   
2. ALCOHOL — Abstain completely during TWW and beyond
   
3. PHYSICAL ACTIVITY
   ▸ Increase to moderate exercise (30min/day walking → 
     light aerobic activity)
   ▸ Avoid intense exercise post-transfer
```

### Future Cycle Planning

```
ADDITIONAL WORKUP TO CONSIDER:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
□ Sperm DNA fragmentation test (SDF/DFI)
  → Critical given male factor diagnosis
  → If DFI >25%: antioxidant therapy, ICSI-IMSI consideration
  
□ AMH testing — baseline ovarian reserve documentation

□ Strict Kruger morphology reporting on next semen analysis

□ If implantation failure occurs:
  → ERA (Endometrial Receptivity Analysis)
  → Hysteroscopy
  → PGT-A on remaining embryos
  → Thrombophilia panel
  
EMBRYO BANKING:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
□ Excellent reserve — consider banking additional blastocysts
  before pregnancy attempt if patient plans >1 child
  
□ Age 34 — time permits but should not delay significantly
```
